title: Tech Note: Authenticating Access to a Secure Area within a Web Site
author: Jonathan Baltazar
featured_technology: SEND HTML FILE for conditional page routing
4D built-in Password System (Use Passwords / Include 4D Passwords)
On Web Authentication database method (6 parameters, Boolean $0)
GET USER LIST / Is user deleted for 4D user validation

historical_commentary.text: Jonathan Baltazar (4D, Inc.) surveys three approaches to securing pages of a 4D-served website circa 2001: a fully custom, application-level login using the Web Exam sample database and QUERY-based credential checks with SEND HTML FILE routing; 4D's built-in Password System (Use Passwords/Include 4D Passwords in Web Server II settings); and the On Web Authentication database method, which receives the URL, HTTP header/body, client/server IP, and username/password as six parameters and returns a Boolean to accept or reject the connection. All three fundamental strategies (application-level login tables, built-in 4D users, and a custom On Web Authentication hook) remain conceptually valid today, but the specific web-serving stack described — 4D's original built-in Web Server, 4D Link/WebSTAR, nph-cgi4d.exe, and 4DISAPI.dll gateways — has been superseded by 4D's modern web server (based on a completely rewritten HTTP engine) and REST/ORDA-based authentication (session tokens, HTTP Basic/OAuth-style flows), making the specific implementation details here obsolete even though the high-level authentication concepts persist.
related_updates: 4D's web server architecture was substantially rewritten in later 4D versions (moving away from the CGI-era 4D Link/nph-cgi4d.exe/4DISAPI.dll gateway model described here)

Modern 4D web/REST authentication commonly uses session tokens and standard HTTP authentication schemes rather than the On Web Authentication six-parameter method shown, though On Web Authentication itself remains available in current 4D versions
4D's REST/ORDA APIs provide additional, more modern mechanisms for securing programmatic access to data that did not exist in 2001
